newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Frances to pay $466 mln for Credito stake.
newsitem.headline: Frances to pay $466 mln for Credito stake.

text.p: Argentina's Banco Frances, controlled by Spain's Banco de Bilbao Vizcaya, said it will pay $466 million for a 71.8 percent stake in retail bank Banco de Credito Argentino.
The announcement was made by Frances's President Luis Otero Monsegur in a letter to the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange. He added that Credito's net worth stood at $305 million on March 31.
Analysts have said they considered a price of up to $450 million to be reasonable.
Otero Monsegur said the deal was subject to auditing under Argentine accounting principles.

"In the event that auditors make adjustments to (Crdito's) net worth, then the price will be adjusted downwards. In the event that the price adjustments exceed $60 million, then, both the bank (Francs) and the sellers (Crdito) will have the right to rescind the deal," he said.
Otero Monsegur added Crdito will make a $46.6 million deposit as a guarantee against potential liabilities.
Banco Francs is Argentina's third largest private bank after Banco de Galicia and Banco Ro, while Crdito is one of Argentina's top 10 retail banks.

Francs will carry out a $300-$350 million capital increase to finance the purchase, the state-run Tlam news agency quoted an unnamed representative of Bilbao's as saying Tuesday. But Francs Marketing Manager Guillermo Laje told Reuters Tuesday the report was premature.
Analysts say the deal is a strategic move by Banco de Bilbao Vizcaya to widen its retail business in Latin America. (( -- Guillermo Haskel, Buenos Aires newsroom, 541 318-0650))
